t.d: Finishing oysters in shallow clay ponds left from old salt marshes, where Blue Navicula algae colours the gills green.
t.tech: affinage in claires, 28 days up to 8 months
t.mat: clay ponds, tidal fresh and salt water

t.r: Cantabria and the Basque Country, Spain
t.d: Hand-processed canning of bonito del norte and anchovies on the Bay of Biscay coast, in oil or escabeche.
t.tech: loins cooked in salt water, cleaned by hand, packed in olive oil or escabeche and sterilised in an autoclave
t.auth: check the can names Thunnus alalunga, not atún claro

t.d: Hand-prepared tinned sardines, tuna and mackerel in olive oil, with aged vintage tins valued like wine.
t.tech: fish cut and gutted by hand, steamed outside the can, packed in tinplate and aged at least six months
t.mat: sardines, tuna, carapau, cod, octopus, olive oil, tinplate
t.auth: look for aged reserve tins and ANICP member producers

t.d: Baltic sprats smoked on alder and canned in oil under a producers' logo.
t.tech: alder smoking then canning in oil
t.auth: the Riga Sprats in Oil logo of the member association

t.d: Salt-curing of spring-caught Cantabrian anchovies for at least six months before filleting and packing in olive oil.
t.tech: clean, salt, cure six months or more, wash, fillet by hand, pack in olive oil
t.auth: fillets firm but flexible, 9 to 12 cm, only anchovies, olive oil and salt; kept chilled

t.r: Caspian and Black Sea, Iran and Russia
t.d: Salt-cured roe of wild beluga, ossetra and sevruga sturgeon, the traditional meaning of caviar, now replaced largely by farmed roe.
t.tech: ovaries removed, sieved, rinsed, salted malossol-style, graded and tinned
t.mat: beluga, ossetra and sevruga roe, salt

t.d: Caviar from sturgeon raised, farmed and slaughtered in France after wild Gironde fishing was banned.
t.tech: Siberian sturgeon farmed up to nine years, roe graded grain by grain and lightly salted
t.auth: Caviar d'Aquitaine collective trademark (2013), IGP in preparation

t.r: Portugal, with fish from Norway and Iceland
t.d: Dry-salted cod, a Portuguese staple adopted from Basque salting off Newfoundland.
t.auth: TSG label Bacalhau de Cura Tradicional Portuguesa

t.d: Skrei hung to dry outdoors for about three months, Norway's oldest food export still traded.
t.tech: open-air racks, cold wind, then sorting into 20-plus grades

t.d: Baltic herring brined then canned to ferment further, sold from the third Thursday of August.
t.tech: caught May and June, brined, headed and gutted, barrelled at 15 to 18 C, canned early July
